title: oncall-handoff-notes-jamie-chen
content:
On-call handoff notes - Jamie Chen (weekend rotation)
Shift dates covered: 2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-03

Context / quick summary:
- Quiet night overall. One medium latency spike (see Incident 1) affecting hosted-api region-us-west-2; mitigated by temporary routing to fallback small-llama variant and increasing dedicated pool by 2 nodes.
- Noted recurring OOMs on model-x when sequence length > 4096; added short-term mitigation steps below.
- Draft runbook sections updated for kv-cache and model rollback; still WIP.

Incidents:
1) Incident: high tail latency (2026-03-02 03:15-03:42 UTC)
   - Impact: hosted-api text-generation requests to model: redwood/gptx-7b caused 95th pct latency 1.2s -> 4.8s for ~30% of requests
   - Detection: latency alert from prometheus rule SLO-Latency-95 (pager triggered)
   - Root cause hypothesis: sudden spike in concurrent long-context inference workload + hot shard on dedicated pool node 
   - Actions taken:
     * 03:18 UTC: temporarily updated routing policy to prefer fallback: redwood/gptx-7b-quant (lower memory) for non-enterprise tenants (command: rctl routes set --model=gptx-7b-quant --policy=cost-priority --scope=hosted)
     * 03:22 UTC: scaled dedicated pool 'dp-us-west-2-1' by +2 nodes (infra-autoscaler override)
     * 03:30 UTC: cleared prefix KV cache on suspected node (see kv-cache clear snippet below)
   - Resolution: service latency returned to baseline by 03:42 UTC. Postmortem ticket: JIRA:INF-1123 (link above).

2) Incident: intermittent OOMs on model-x (ongoing, low frequency)
   - Observed: OOM kills in serving-runtime logs when seq_len > 4096 on quantized pathway
   - Temporary mitigation applied: enforce request-level max_seq_len=4096 for model-x via request filter in routing layer (config pushed 2026-03-02 11:05 UTC)
   - Next steps: schedule follow-up with applied-ml to evaluate quantization profile; see SRE-789.

Open items / TODOs:
- TODO: flesh out runbook step for automatic fallback routing policy (owner: Riley) - ticket SRE-812
- TODO: add monitoring to detect hot shard imbalance earlier (owner: Ayesha)
- TODO: update Confluence runbook for kv-cache management with exact kubectl commands and pod labels
- Low priority: verify rollback test for model variant switching under load (add synthetic workload job)

Temporary procedures (keepsakes until runbook finalized):
- Quick mitigation for high tail latency:
  1) Confirm alerts: prometheus -> alert manager -> paging. Check details in alert UI.
  2) If latency spike corresponds to a single model: update routing to fallback quantized model or lower-quality variant. Command example: rctl routes set --model=<fallback-model> --policy=latency-priority --scope=region:<region>
  3) If request backlog is large: scale dedicated pool by +1 or +2 nodes via infra-autoscaler override: infractl scale --pool <pool-name> --delta +2
  4) If immediate memory pressure suspected: clear prefix KV cache on offending node (see below).

- KV cache clear snippet (temporary admin-only):
  * Purpose: free up runtime KV caches that can cause OOM when many long-context requests spike. Use with caution: will reduce cache hit-rate temporarily.
  * Commands (k8s):
    - kubectl get pods -n serving | grep <node-pod-pattern>
    - kubectl exec -n serving <pod> -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/kv/clear
    - watch logs: kubectl logs -n serving <pod> -c runtime --since=5m | grep "kv-cache"
  * Notes: avoid mass-clearing across all pods unless rolling strategy used. Prefer clearing single suspected hot pod first.

Escalation contacts (order):
- On-call SRE (primary): Jamie Chen (you are AI reading this) - pager/Slack: @jamie.sre - mobile: +1-555-0103
- SRE lead: Riley Patel - slack: @riley - mobile: +1-555-0147
- Applied ML lead (model issues): Ayesha Singh - slack: @ayesha - mobile: +1-555-0199
- Platform infra: Noah Martinez - slack: @noah - mobile: +1-555-0122

Runbook snippets to be merged into Confluence:
- Latency spike playbook: detection -> isolate model -> route to fallback -> scale pool -> clear KV cache -> monitor -> postmortem
- Rollback model variant: commands for routing override and verification:
    rctl routes set --model=<stable-variant> --policy=latency-priority --scope=all
    rctl routes get --model=<stable-variant> --format=json | jq '.routes'
    // verify with smoke test: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate -d '{"input":"smoke test"}' | jq '.latency'

Notes to next shift (bullet style):
- Watch for any follow-ups on INF-1123 and SRE-789; both have actions assigned but not yet closed.
- If you need to perform a KV cache clear, coordinate with platform on-call to avoid clearing more than one pod in the same shard at once.
- Keep an eye on model-x seq_len metrics: metric key model_x.seq_len.max and model_x.oom.count
- If you see sustained 95p latency >2s for >10 minutes, start escalation immediately per above contacts.

Personal scratchpad thoughts (informal):
- Might be worth adding a short-circuit in routing to detect per-tenant long-context bursts and apply tenant-level rate limits to protect shared pools. TODO: sketch in product backlog.
- Consider adding synthetic canary jobs that exercise long-context paths every N minutes to catch memory pressure before customer traffic does.

Appendix: useful links and quick references
- Alert dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/alerts/oncall
- Incident ticket INF-1123: https://jira.redwood.internal/browse/INF-1123
- Runbook draft on Confluence: confluence://runbooks/latency-spike-playbook
- Slack channel: #sre-oncall

End of handoff notes.

-- Jamie C.
